reader.requirement: At --std 85, the SEARCH Format 1 VARYING identifier-2 must be a USAGE INDEX data item or a numeric elementary item with no positions right of the assumed decimal point (so 99PP and S99 are legal, 9V9, PP9, alphanumeric, numeric-edited and groups are not), and must not be subscripted by the first index-name of identifier-1's INDEXED BY phrase; the compiler must refuse each violation.

edition-consulted.switches: DialectBehavior.SearchIndexBelowTableUnsuccessful: the run-time lower bound of the start test (1985 GR2 has none); not the identifier-2 screen

reader.edition-search: grep Edition|CobolVersion|DialectBehavior in SearchBinder.cs, OperandClassScreen.cs and SubscriptBinder.SubscriptNamesIndex; the class screen and the subscript test consult no edition.
reader.witnesses-cover: part: the witness is the GO TO / SET operand-class screen sibling; the SEARCH VARYING class arms, the 99PP and S99 accept arms and the first-index subscript prohibition are exercised only by the probes here

probes.printed: EXIT 0; S=+03 (S99 varied with the search), Q=0000 (99PP accepted), XI-FOUND (USAGE INDEX), END, F2=12 (F (KX) subscripted by the second index-name accepted and incremented)
COBOL2325 for D (9V9, not an integer), A (alphanumeric), P (PP9, not an integer), GR (group), NE (numeric-edited), F (JX) and E (IX) (subscripted by the first index-name)
probes.expected: refused per SR2 first and second sentences

citations.check: OK  §1985:VI.6.22.3 SR2  (║6.22.3 Syntax Rules║)  the text is in SR2

reader.notes: The 1985 wording 'without any positions to the right of the assumed decimal point' matches the integer-description predicate the screen uses: 99PP is admitted and PP9 refused. The subscript prohibition compares the index declaration by identity, so the second index-name of the same table is legal.
